tagline: Set your hours, share a link, fill your calendar.
intro: Book is scheduling without setup. The first time you open it, a personal calendar appears and you can start adding events, while behind the scenes Book turns your working hours into free time slots that power public booking pages and agent-driven meeting-finding. This chapter walks you from your weekly hours to a shared booking link, takes you through the cross-app Timeline that pulls Bam tasks and Bond deals alongside your events, and shows where an AI agent can do the scheduling math that has no human screen yet. By the end you will be able to publish a link an outside visitor can book, and know exactly which controls are live and which are still being finished.
atAGlance: A personal calendar provisioned automatically, with Week, Day, and Month views
Working hours that compute free slots for availability and public booking pages
Public booking links at /book/meet/<slug> that outsiders can use without logging in
A cross-app Timeline that gathers Book events, Bam task due dates, and Bond deal close dates
An agent can find a common free time across several people, the math Book has no screen for

pullQuotes.after: subtracts the events that mark you as busy, and produces free time slots
pullQuotes.text: Working hours minus busy events equals availability, and that availability powers every booking page you publish.

pullQuotes.after: finding a common free time across several people
pullQuotes.text: An agent can intersect everyone's calendars and hand back a meeting time, the one scheduling job Book has no human screen for.

callouts.after: paste a public iCalendar URL and Book mirrors
callouts.text: Google and Outlook two-way sync stay disabled until an operator supplies OAuth credentials, but the .ics path needs nothing. Most calendar apps, including Google and Outlook, can publish a public .ics URL for any calendar you own, so paste that and Book mirrors it in with no setup.

callouts.after: defaults to on at the data layer, new pages create a Bond contact
callouts.text: The booking-page editor exposes only title, slug, description, duration, buffers, and brand color. Because auto_create_bond_contact defaults to on at the data layer and the editor has no toggle for it, every new page creates or updates a Bond contact by email on each booking. To change that, set the flag with the book_update_booking_page MCP tool.

callouts.after: The save replaces your full weekly schedule with the enabled days shown
callouts.text: Saving Working Hours is a full replace, not a merge. The save overwrites your entire weekly schedule with whatever days are currently enabled, so any day you forgot to re-enable is dropped. Confirm every day you want available is checked before you click Save Working Hours.

callouts.after: guarded by a row lock, and a collision returns a 409
callouts.text: Set your Working Hours, create a booking page with a unique lowercase slug, then open its /book/meet/<slug> link in a private window and book yourself a slot. Watch the confirmed event land on your default calendar.

quiz.q: What is created for you automatically the first time you open Book, and can it be deleted?
choices: A team calendar; yes, it can be deleted
A personal calendar named My Calendar; no, it cannot be deleted
A booking page; yes, it can be deleted
Nothing is created until you add a calendar
quiz.answer: A personal calendar named My Calendar; no, it cannot be deleted

quiz.q: What status and visibility does a brand-new event get by default?
choices: status tentative, visibility free
status confirmed, visibility busy
status confirmed, visibility free
status cancelled, visibility out_of_office

quiz.q: When you cancel an event, what actually happens to it?
quiz.answer: Cancelling is a soft delete: the event's status flips to cancelled rather than the row being erased, so it drops out of availability and the timeline but its record is retained.
quiz.where: Key concepts: Event, and Story: Cancel an event

quiz.q: Which event visibility setting does NOT consume an availability slot?
choices: Busy
Free
Tentative
Out of Office

quiz.q: What are the default working hours when you first set up Book?
quiz.answer: Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00, are enabled by default.
quiz.where: Key concepts: Working hours, and the Working Hours feature

quiz.q: Where does the event created by a public booking land?
choices: On a new calendar created for the booking
As a confirmed event on the page owner's default calendar
On the visitor's calendar
Nowhere until the owner accepts it
quiz.answer: As a confirmed event on the page owner's default calendar
quiz.where: Key concepts: Booking, and Public Meet page

quiz.q: Which two controls appear on the New Event form but do nothing when you save, and why?
quiz.answer: The Reminder dropdown and the Color picker. Book has no reminder feature or job, and event color is not stored on the event because color lives on the calendar, so both controls are inactive.
quiz.where: New Event and Edit Event: Notes and current limitations

quiz.q: What happens if you choose a Repeat option like Weekly on an event?
choices: Book generates all future occurrences immediately
The rule is stored on the single event but not expanded, so it remains one event
The event is rejected as unsupported
It creates a recurring booking page
quiz.answer: The rule is stored on the single event but not expanded, so it remains one event
quiz.where: New Event and Edit Event: Notes and current limitations

quiz.q: Which calendar feed provider works today with no credentials, and which two require operator-supplied OAuth before they can be connected?
quiz.answer: The .ics feed provider works with no credentials; Google Calendar and Microsoft Outlook require operator-supplied OAuth credentials before a connection can be created.
quiz.where: Connections, and Key concepts: External connection

quiz.q: Roughly how often does the background sweep refresh every .ics connection on its own?
choices: Every minute
Every fifteen minutes
Once an hour
Once a day

quiz.q: What does disconnecting an .ics feed do to the events Book pulled from it?
quiz.answer: Disconnecting removes the connection and every event Book mirrored from that feed, so the calendar returns to just your own events.
quiz.where: Connections: How sync works, and Key concepts: Synced (mirrored) event

quiz.q: When two visitors try to grab the same booking slot at once, what stops a double-booking?
choices: The slot is simply offered to both
A row lock guards the booking, and a collision returns a 409 'This time slot is no longer available'
The second visitor is silently dropped
Both bookings are created and merged later
quiz.answer: A row lock guards the booking, and a collision returns a 409 'This time slot is no longer available'

quiz.q: Why can't you add attendees from the human New Event form, and how can attendees be added instead?
quiz.answer: The human form does not support adding or editing attendees; attendees are set when an event is created through the API or an agent tool, book_create_event.
quiz.where: New Event and Edit Event: Notes, and Working with AI agents
